newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania OTC market rises, growth seen ahead.
newsitem.headline: Romania OTC market rises, growth seen ahead.

text.p: Romania's over-the-counter (OTC) market saw growing volumes this week and system officials anticipate further growth on the back of foreign investment.
Turnover in five days of trading almost quadrupled to 12.1 billion lei on the previous week, as did the volume, which stood at more than 4.0 million shares.

RASDAQ system officials say the market -- which lists 2,319 stocks and this week traded a daily average of 150 stocks -- is bound to pick up as more stocks join in and foreign investors start taking an interest in Romanian equities.
The RASDAQ, modelled on the U.S. NASDAQ exchange, will eventually trade shares in 5,000 companies.
"Shortly, in one or two months, I see a substantial RASDAQ participation of foreign buyers and volumes will fly even higher," system manager Mihai Catuneanu said.
Some brokers said they had already been contacted by foreigners eager to put their money in Romanian stocks.
"Foreign investors seem encouraged by political changes, by the new government's commitment to improve the capital market," said a trader.
Romania's new ruling centrist coalition which ousted leftists in last November's polls, has pledged support to develop capital markets and draw in foreign investment.

A stock exchange, in operation since late 1995, trades 17 stocks. It was sluggish throughout 1996 but has recovered this year in what traders say is heavy interest from foreign investors and local institutional buyers.
But volumes on the bourse, which traded 105,506 shares on Thursday, remain scant in comparison with the OTC.

Analysts say the bourse needs more listings to gain in liquidity. Some blame its modest performance on a market regulator rule compelling companies privatised under a 1996 mass selloff to sign up with the shareholders' registry.
"That register is compatible only with the OTC market, not with the bourse," said one analyst.
But Catuneanu dismissed the complaint. "RASDAQ-listed companies can move to the bourse if they wish. And some of them did but gave up because of tedious bourse listing procedures."
"There's room for both the exchange and the RASDAQ. The important thing is that the market operates to send the right signals to local and foreign investors," a broker said.
